reading.title: Looking After Your Health
reading.text: Our teacher gave us a talk about health yesterday. She said that most people in good health follow a healthy diet and take regular exercise. She also explained that mental health is as important as physical health. Friends, hobbies and enough sleep can all improve your health. On the other hand, too much fast food and too little sleep can damage your health. She told us to visit the health centre if we have any health problems. At the end she asked us to write one rule for looking after our health. I wrote: walk to school every day.

reading.title: Fighting Diseases
reading.text: A hundred years ago, many people died of diseases that doctors can cure today. Better hospitals, clean water and vaccines have changed the world. A disease can spread through the air, through dirty water or through insects. For example, a cold is a viral infection that moves from person to person very quickly. Bacteria can also cause infections, such as a throat infection, and doctors may give antibiotics for them. To prevent disease, we should wash our hands, eat healthy food and visit the doctor for regular check-ups. If we all do this, we can keep our families and our communities safe.

reading.title: Why We Say No
reading.text: At school we had a health lesson about smoking and illegal drugs. The teacher explained that smoking harms the lungs and the heart, and it can lead to serious illnesses in later life. Passive smoking is also dangerous because other people breathe the smoke. Illegal drugs are even more harmful, because they can damage the brain and the body, and people may become addicted. She talked about peer pressure, when friends try to make you do something you do not want to do. It is brave to say no, and real friends will respect that. If anyone feels worried, they should talk to a parent, a teacher or call a helpline for free advice.
